hist.established_mechanism:
The V-ATPase false negatives come from two independent layers. Fixing one layer alone does not change any call.

(1) GPR layer.
- The current model m059 keeps the inherited rule (12-gene AND, including a-candidate YALI1E12482g) OR (YALI1F38820g AND YALI1F13017g).
- Verified this run with Boolean evaluation on m059: no single KO of any of the 14 genes makes the R794 or R795 GPR false. The 11 consensus-essential genes (A11258, E14125, E10492, A09766, F20965, F31854, F21690, E37063, E32332, E12482, F13017) therefore never close either reaction.
- The 09-10 3-gene AND hypothesis put the AND only on the 3 non-consensus genes (D00581, E16192, F38820; verified non-membership this run). It left the 11 E genes hidden by the inner OR.
- The 09-21 candidate, 12 shared AND (E12482 OR F38820), does propagate KOs of the 12 shared genes to R794.

(2) Network/objective layer (decisive).
- Even when R794/R795 are closed, KO/WT is about 1. The WT optimum already has R794 = R795 = 0, so the KO feasible set still contains the WT optimum (monotonicity argument, verified in the 09-10, 09-21 and 10-28 reports).
- Nothing in the objective or constraints needs Golgi or vacuolar H+. biomass_C has no C_go/C_va species (verified on m059 this run). There is no pH, membrane-potential, storage or acid-dependent-process term.
- The H+ rows are pure balances that the all-zero solution satisfies. Vacuolar H+ is used only for transport.
- R795 is [0,0], inherited from iYali4 (2016) with no recorded motive. Opening it alone, or with R1363, gives max flux 0. The reasons: R1363 closed; dipeptide exchanges secretion-only; R871/R876/R883 closed; so 2*v_R795 = 0.
- Opening everything (UM2 options B, B', C, C') only frees ATP-burning futile cycles, with pFBA 0 and 0 KO class changes. R1163 as written creates a loop.
- Artificial dipeptide supply makes R795 carry flux only for the extra growth. With the pump closed, base growth persists at 86.17% (pool) or about 99.65% (E5 bounded) of WT, so no 15% call flips.
- R1159 is not an active bypass (0 in WT; now [-1000,0]).
- The model already has a free ATP-hydrolysis sink, R_NTP1 (verified on m059: [0,1000], ATP + H2O -> ADP + Pi). Pump-based ATP dissipation adds no capability.
- Project conclusion (UM2 report, 10-28): the 11 FN 'come from a missing acidification requirement, not from the closure'. In the FN classification (10-27) all 11 are category d, 'unused_at_optimum:v_atpase'.

Biology (homology/screen level only; no native name verified):
- The Y. lipolytica vacuolar H+-ATPase is active (Kulakovskaya 1993; abstract re-read by an earlier session).
- The core subunits are essential in the PO1f CRISPR screens.
- The essential a-subunit is YALI1E12482g, which is the reverse-best hit of STV1 though its forward best hit is VPH1. The VPH1-RBH YALI1F38820g is non-essential in both screens.
open_questions: How to represent a growth-linked acidification requirement with evidence. Options: a biomass- or growth-coupled vacuolar/Golgi H+ demand, a pH/membrane-potential constraint, a vacuolar storage term, or coupling of Golgi glycosylation or secretion to H+. The required evidence is the measured or literature-derived stoichiometry and the condition. None has been designed or tested; the 10-28 TASK.md lists this as follow-up 4: 'would need evidence-based constraints, not a recall target'.

Even with a demand added, the 12 shared-component KOs become lethal only if no other route can satisfy it. Candidate escapes: R1159 (now [-1000,0]), R1163 (closed; uphill as written), the other H+-coupled transports, and the R_NTP1 free hydrolysis sink. Not tested (inferred).

Compartment-specific a-subunit assignment. YALI1E12482g is essential and STV1 reverse-RBH; YALI1F38820g is VPH1-RBH and non-essential (Cas9 q 1, Cas12a q 0.31). Under the 09-21 candidate (E12482 OR F38820), E12482's KO would still not close the reactions, so E12482 would stay FN (inferred from the Boolean form). Which a serves R794 (Golgi) vs R795 (vacuole) is unresolved.
W29 F-subunit identity. The old YALI0E16192g (CLIB122) maps to W29 YALI1E19360g, annotated as a pseudogene with a frameshift. This blocks a formal shared-AND rule.
Whether c'' (YALI1F13017g) belongs in the shared AND. Structural and BLAST support exists; no native data.

- R794 V-ATPase: [0,1000]; ATP-coupled pump, cy to go. The only reaction that can supply net H+ into the Golgi.
- R1159 H+ diffusion cy<-go: [-1000,0]; passive leak, go to cy only (curated 2026-09-23). Golgi H+ sink.

claims.claim: Calcium-sensitive Pet- (respiration-deficient) cls mutants are V-ATPase mutants (CLS7 = VMA3, CLS8 = VMA1). They have about 6-fold higher cytosolic Ca2+ (900 vs 150 nM) and lost vacuolar Ca2+ uptake, yet no detectable mitochondrial defect.

claims.claim: Mechanism of respiratory failure: V-ATPase-deficient cells (vma mutants or concanamycin A) grow on fermentable carbon but not on glycerol. Loss of vacuolar acidity lets cysteine leave the vacuole, and non-vacuolar cysteine causes oxidant-dependent intracellular iron limitation. This activates the Aft1 iron regulon and starves Fe-S-dependent respiration. Iron supplementation, FET4 overexpression, ROX1 deletion, cysteine depletion, or SOD1+TSA1 overexpression restore respiratory growth; AFT1 loss is lethal in V-ATPase-deficient cells.
claims.quote_or_passage: Hughes et al. 2020 Cell, Results (paraphrase from the full text read via efetch): V-ATPase mutants or concA-treated cells grew efficiently on fermentable carbon but failed on glycerol; FET4 was the single high-copy suppressor; ferrous iron restored respiratory growth; loss of AFT1 was lethal in V-ATPase-deficient cells and rescued by iron; the Fig. 7 model has the V-ATPase gradient driving amino acid/H+ antiporters that store cysteine in the vacuole.

claims.claim: vma2 deletion mutants grown at permissive pH 5 show chronic endogenous oxidative stress and induce the Aft1/Aft2 iron regulon. Respiration is not the main source of their ROS.
claims.quote_or_passage: Milgrom et al. 2007 JBC abstract (paraphrase): vma2Delta has elevated ROS and oxidative protein damage without added oxidant; rho0 did not relieve it; microarrays at pH 5 showed up-regulation of Aft1/Aft2 iron regulon genes and TSA2.

claims.claim: Loss of V-ATPase gives an iron-deprivation signal (P_FIT2-GFP induction) even though total cell iron in vma2Delta is replete. Iron supplementation suppresses the signal.
claims.quote_or_passage: Diab & Kane 2013 JBC abstract (paraphrase): both biosensors were up-regulated in vma2Delta; total iron measurements show the mutant is iron-replete despite iron-regulon up-regulation; iron supplementation decreased P_FIT2-GFP.

claims.claim: A genome-wide screen for growth on iron-restricted medium found that cwh36 (later identified as a V0 subunit, YCL005W-A) cells cannot load copper into apo-Fet3p, which links V-ATPase to high-affinity iron uptake.
claims.quote_or_passage: Davis-Kaplan et al. 2004 JBC abstract (paraphrase): Deltacwh36 had a severe growth defect on iron-limited medium and could not copper-load apoFet3p; the V-ATPase is not assembled in these cells; the ORF is YCL005W-A.

claims.claim: Vacuolar acidity falls early in replicative aging and limits mitochondrial function. This works through reduced pH-dependent amino acid storage in the vacuole, not through vacuolar proteolysis.
claims.quote_or_passage: Hughes & Gottschling 2012 Nature abstract (paraphrase): vacuolar pH changes limit mitochondrial function by reducing pH-dependent amino acid storage in the vacuolar lumen, not by disrupting protein degradation.

lit.ylipolytica_direct_evidence:
No targeted V-ATPase mutant study exists for Y. lipolytica that I could find. I searched Europe PMC titles and abstracts and ran one web search. Every piece of direct evidence comes from genome-wide pooled screens:
- Hermes Tn-seq: Patterson 2018, strain CLIB89.
- Validated Cas9 library: Schwartz 2019, strain PO1f, minimal medium with 2% glucose.
- Cas9 and Cas12a screens analysed with acCRISPR: Ramesh 2023, strain PO1f, SD-Leu with 2% glucose.

The consensus list (1,612 genes essential in at least 2 of 3 screens) is the benchmark. None of these papers discusses V-ATPase in its main text; the gene-level calls are in their supplements.

From the local raw fitness table, verified this run:
- 11 of the 14 GPR genes on R794/R795 are consensus-essential.
- Several have very strong Cas9 fitness defects: YALI1F13017g (VMA16/PPA1-like) FS -5.88, YALI1E32332g (VMA2-like) -5.46, YALI1E12482g (STV1-like a subunit) -5.22.
- Three of the 11 are essential in Cas9 but not in Cas12a: E10492g, E32332g and F21690g. Under the 2-of-3 rule they must also have been essential in the Hermes screen. That is inferred; Patterson Table S3 was not read.
- YALI1F38820g, the Vph1-like a-subunit candidate in the 2-gene OR branch, is nonessential in both CRISPR screens (Cas9 q=1.0, Cas12a q=0.31). The STV1-like YALI1E12482g is strongly essential. So the alternative a-subunit gives no detectable redundancy in vivo on glucose, unlike the partial VPH1/STV1 redundancy seen in S. cerevisiae and C. albicans. This is inferred: paralog annotation is by similarity only and no localisation data exist.
- YALI1D00581g is a borderline nonessential (Cas9 p=0.049, q=0.17). YALI0E16192g has no YALI1 screen row.

The screen papers report no culture pH. The medium is unbuffered YNB-based SD-Leu, so the cells were not at the pH 7.5 that kills S. cerevisiae vma mutants. That points to a respiration- or iron-linked cause of lethality in this obligate aerobe, not pH lethality (inferred).

The only other Y. lipolytica-specific source is biochemical (Kulakovskaya 1993): log-phase vacuoles have high V-ATPase activity and build a proton gradient and membrane potential.
essentiality_mechanisms: Loss of vacuolar acidification is pH-conditionally lethal. S. cerevisiae vma mutants do not grow above pH 6.5 and grow well only near pH 5.5, probably because low external pH lets endocytosis acidify the vacuole (Nelson & Nelson 1990, verified abstract). Mutants fail at pH 7.5 (Manolson 1994; Sambade 2005, verified abstracts). Filamentous fungi show the same: N. crassa vma-1 does not grow at pH 7.0 or above; A. nidulans vmaA is not viable above pH 7 (verified abstracts).

Respiratory failure (the Pet- part of the phenotype): vma mutants cannot use glycerol or other nonfermentable carbon (Manolson 1994, Ohya 1991, Sambade 2005, verified abstracts). Hughes 2020 (verified full text) gives the mechanism: the V-ATPase gradient drives amino acid/H+ antiporters that store cysteine in the vacuole. Without it, cytosolic cysteine causes oxidant-dependent iron limitation, starving Fe-S-dependent respiration. Iron, FET4 overexpression, cysteine depletion or antioxidants rescue respiratory growth, and AFT1 loss is synthetically lethal. In an obligate aerobe such as Y. lipolytica, which cannot ferment, this conditional phenotype would become lethal on any carbon source (inferred).

Iron uptake and iron signalling: V0 subunit loss (cwh36/YCL005W-A) blocks copper loading of apo-Fet3p, so high-affinity iron uptake fails (Davis-Kaplan 2004). vma mutants constitutively activate the Aft1 iron regulon (Milgrom 2007; Diab & Kane 2013). Verified abstracts.
Chronic endogenous oxidative stress: vma2Delta has elevated ROS and protein oxidation even at permissive pH 5 (Milgrom 2007, verified abstract).

Ca2+ and metal detoxification: V-ATPase-driven H+/Ca2+ and H+/metal antiport loads the vacuole. vma mutants have about 6-fold higher cytosolic Ca2+ (Ohya 1991) and are sensitive to 100 mM CaCl2 and 4 mM ZnCl2 (Manolson 1994). Zn2+ sensitivity is also seen in N. crassa, A. nidulans, A. niger, C. albicans and M. oryzae (verified abstracts).
Amino acid storage in the vacuole: pH-dependent amino acid storage, not proteolysis, links vacuolar pH to mitochondrial function (Hughes & Gottschling 2012, verified abstract).

Morphogenesis and cell wall: severe tip-growth, branching, sporulation and cell-wall defects in N. crassa, A. nidulans, A. niger and M. oryzae (verified abstracts). These are non-metabolic, so FBA cannot represent them.

Range across fungi: essential or near-lethal in N. crassa (RIP inactivation inviable without rescue; a hypomorph grows slowly) and in A. nidulans and A. niger (extremely or very poor growth). Viable but conditional in S. cerevisiae, S. pombe, C. albicans (Crabtree-negative, still viable on glucose), A. oryzae and M. oryzae (which lacks pH-conditional lethality). Essential on glucose in Y. lipolytica by genome-wide screens. No data were found for K. lactis.
lit.how_other_gems_handle_it:
All checked this run:

- **Yeast-GEM (main, commit 2d594ae):** V-ATPase is two reactions. r_1085 (Golgi) has a 16-gene AND rule that includes STV1, and r_1086 (vacuole) has one that includes VPH1. Each also has an alternative branch that drops only YPR170W-B. Vacuolar and Golgi 'H+ diffusion' (r_1831, r_1826) run freely in both directions (-1000 to 1000). Nothing in the network requires a vacuolar proton gradient. The Yeast8 paper does not mention V-ATPase and scores essentiality against complete-medium deletion data, where vma mutants are viable anyway.
- **iYali (SysBioChalmers W29-GEM, 2021):** y001085 and y001086 use one 13-gene AND rule with no OR branch. Vacuolar and Golgi H+ diffusion are again reversible. So no single V-ATPase knockout can be lethal in FBA there either (inferred, no LP run).
- **Recon3D:** one lysosomal reaction, ATPasel_1. Its GPR is an OR of 5-gene isoform combinations, not the whole complex.
- **Published methods:** none found that captures V-ATPase essentiality.
  - Thermodynamic methods (Haraldsdóttir 2012 for Recon 1; Thermo-Flux 2026) use compartment pH and membrane potential only to set reaction directionality. Thermo-Flux defaults to pH 7 and 0 mV.
  - AcidifyME (an E. coli ME-model) models pH effects on lipids, periplasmic proteins and membrane-protein activity, not proton pumps.
  - pcYeast and StressME have no V-ATPase terms.

**Contrast with iYali26 m059 (verified static read):**
- R794 and R795 share the 12-gene complex OR a 2-gene (YALI1F38820g AND YALI1F13017g) branch. That branch has no counterpart in iYali or Yeast-GEM, and the screens do not support it: F38820g is nonessential in both CRISPR screens.
- R795 (vacuole) and the vacuolar H+ diffusion R1163 are both fixed at 0. Golgi H+ leaves only through R1159.
- So the false negatives have two layers: the GPR bypass, and no flux requirement on V-ATPase at all. Fixing only the GPR would probably not change KO/WT (inferred, no LP run).

**Options ranked by defensibility (all inferred recommendations; none authorized or tested here):**
1. **Classify as out of scope.** Treat the 11 genes as mechanistically out-of-scope false negatives for FBA (non-metabolic: pH, Ca2+/metal, iron-signalling and respiratory-support functions), and report them separately rather than forcing the model. This needs no model change and fits the benchmark's no-recall-tuning rule.
2. **Correct the GPR on its own evidence.** Re-examine the (F38820g AND F13017g) branch for identity and complex-composition reasons alone, since the screens contradict its redundancy, and decide whether an STV1/VPH1 split like Yeast-GEM's is supported. This is a GPR-correctness change; by itself it will not fix the false negatives.
3. **Mechanistic coupling, only with independent evidence.**
   - Make a required process depend on organelle acidification. Candidates are high-affinity Fe uptake via Fet3 copper loading (Davis-Kaplan 2004), or vacuolar storage of amino acids and cysteine (Hughes 2012/2020).
   - Alternatively, give vacuolar H+ a measured non-zero leak or maintenance term.
   - Any such constraint needs quantitative Y. lipolytica data (vacuolar pH, H+ leak, iron uptake route) and must not be tuned to recall. AGENTS.md forbids adding demands or closing bypasses merely to improve recall.
   - It should be checked against the S. cerevisiae conditional phenotypes: viable at pH 5.5 on glucose, lethal on glycerol and at pH 7.5.

No published GEM precedent for options 2 or 3 was found.

Scope and inputs, verified this run:
- Model: m059.xml, SHA-256 059316ef…a9248d. Loaded with cobra; no LP was run.
- Consensus list: SHA 1e887f5a…659b, 1612 genes.
- Cas9/Cas12a long table: SHA 97ef5596…d9ff.
- S2 YALI1/YALI0 locus map: SHA 42658fb9…a670.
- Gene identification: one regex scan of every annotation line in the S2 locus map for S. cerevisiae V-ATPase gene names and systematic ORFs. The script is at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-david-Desktop-Lab-Ian-wheeldon-code-iyali26-gem--claude-worktrees-essential-gene-prediction-e76be3/0a4ec4c9-d926-4768-b75c-c14c6fe4ecec/scratchpad/vat/agents/scan_annot.py, and the table script is vat_table.py in the same folder.
- Subunit labels are homology annotations only. No native name is verified.
- Benchmark definition: model genes not on the list count as non-essential, a user-defined negative class.

1) The 11 FNs. R794 and R795 carry 14 genes. Of these, 11 are consensus E: A, B, C, E, G, H, a1 (E12482), c, c', c'' and d [verified]. The other 3 are D, F (old ID YALI0E16192g) and a2 (F38820), and none of them is on the list [verified].

Model state [verified]:
- Both reactions use the GPR (12 genes: A C G D H E F c d c' B a1) OR (a2 AND c'').
- R795 bounds are [0,0]; R794 bounds are [0,1000].
- A Boolean evaluation of the GPR for every one of the 14 single knockouts leaves it TRUE. So no single subunit knockout can ever close these reactions.
- The rule contradicts the data. Branch 2 needs only a2 and c''. But a2 is non-essential in both screens, and c'' is the most strongly essential gene in the set (Cas9 q 1.4e-14, Cas12a q 3.9e-9). Branch 1 also lacks c'' completely, so knocking out c'' is bypassed through branch 1.

2) Is the experimental data consistent? Mostly yes. Every core subunit with a scorable single W29 locus is consensus essential except D: A, B, C, E, G, H, a1, c, c', c'', d and e, which is 12 of the 13 scorable core-subunit loci [verified].

The pattern also fits a two-isoform 'a' subunit: a1 is strongly essential and a2 is non-essential in both screens [verified data; isoform interpretation inferred]. Assembly factors VMA21, PKR1 and RAV1 are consensus E, VPH2 is split, and the putative VOA1 is non-essential [verified]. Overall the data say the V-ATPase is required on SD-Leu [inferred].

3) Possible call or mapping problems:
- (a) D, YALI1D00581g (VMA8). Fitness is negative in both screens and the raw p values are 0.049 and 0.015, but q is 0.17 and 0.079, so it is not consensus. A single-copy central-stalk subunit being dispensable while every partner is essential is unlikely. This is likely a screen-sensitivity false call [inferred], not a mapping error: the locus-map annotation is a clear VMA8 match [verified].
- (b) F, YALI0E16192g (VMA7). This is a mapping problem [verified facts, inferred cause]:
  - The model keeps the CLIB122 ID.
  - Its W29 counterpart YALI1E19360g is typed 'Pseudo mRNA'.
  - Neither ID has a Cas9 or Cas12a row (0 matches).
  - The YALI0-only CDS sheet splits it into a 367-bp CDS plus a 2-bp CDS, which looks like a gene-model artefact.
  - Its essentiality is unknown and must not be treated as non-essential. Yet under the benchmark's user-defined negative class it is scored as a negative.
- (c) e, YALI1F25663g (VMA9). Cas9 FS is -5.23 (E) and Cas12a FS is +0.45 (NE): a strong discordance, possibly from Cas12a guide coverage on a small gene [inferred]. It is consensus E but absent from the GEM, so it is an out-of-scope positive, not an FN.
- (d) Consensus E with Cas12a non-essential: B, H, d and RAV1. Their consensus calls must rest on the transposon screen. Per-gene transposon calls are not recovered (benchmark_contract_20260905.md and baseline_manifest), so those votes cannot be shown [verified absence; vote inferred from the 2-of-3 rule].
- (e) No VMA22 or RAV2 locus could be identified from the annotations [verified scan]. This is unknown, not absent.
- (f) The a1 identity is ambiguous: synteny says STV1 (Anc_2.617), while the sequence hit is VPH1 [verified annotation text]. A compartment assignment of a1 vs a2 (Golgi vs vacuole) is not supported by the screen data [inferred].
- (g) Side note: subunit A also sits on R_NTP1 as (A09766g OR E41893g), a generic ATP hydrolysis reaction [verified]. It has no bearing on the V-ATPase FN.

4) What this means for the fix. The data support this rule: core AND (A B C D E F G H c c' c'' d [+ e if added]) AND (a1 OR a2). Making a1 alone required would be a stronger, data-driven claim that needs separate evidence. A GPR fix alone will not create the FNs' growth defect:
- The 2026-09-21 screen of exactly that rule (core AND, a1 OR a2) gave 0 class changes at all cutoffs [recalled from model/reports/screen_vatpase_candidate_20260921/REPORT.md, read this run, not recomputed].

In the earlier Boolean check (findings, verified this run by that agent), none of the 14 single knockouts makes this rule false. All 24 cross-branch pairs do. It has no V1 head, and it contradicts the screens: F38820g is non-essential in both CRISPR screens, while F13017g (c'') is the most strongly essential gene in the set (Cas9 FS -5.88). (verified data; reading of what branch 2 means is inferred)

(2) Network layer, the decisive one. No biomass-linked process in m059 uses Golgi or vacuolar H+:
- biomass_C has no C_go or C_va species. (verified, findings)
- R795 is fixed at [0,0], and the user kept it closed with A0 on 2026-10-28. (verified)

- So the wild-type optimum already has R794 = R795 = 0, and any knockout that closes them still contains that optimum (KO/WT = 1). Shown in the 09-10, 09-21 and 10-28 reports (read; recalled for m059).

New static facts from this run (verified, cobra load of m059, no solver; scripts opt_check4-6.py in the agents scratch folder):
- Cytosolic Fe2+ m948 is produced only by R2193, the high-affinity FET3/FTR1 iron uptake. Its other reactions consume it: R863 (to the mitochondrion), R727 (sirohydrochlorin ferrochelatase) and biomass_C, at 3.04e-5.
- R2193's GPR is (YALI1D09277g AND YALI1D09308g) OR (YALI1D08684g AND YALI1D08564g), a user-authorized change of 2026-10-22.
- Both D09 genes are consensus-essential. They are themselves FN (cause a, 'or_partner_carries_flux') in current_fn_fp.json.
- R2048 (YALIUNK3 placeholder) is reversible, and R1240 moves M(IP)2C between ER and Golgi in both directions. A sphingolipid shuttle could therefore supply Golgi H+ without R794 (inferred from the stoichiometry).
- xMAINTENANCE is [7.8625, 1000] and R_NTP1 is [0,1000]. Both are cytosolic ATP hydrolysis.

Biology:
- Y. lipolytica: there is no targeted V-ATPase mutant study. The direct evidence is the pooled screens (verified CSV rows) and the vacuolar H+-ATPase activity reported by Kulakovskaya 1993 (verified abstract).
- S. cerevisiae: the V-ATPase links to growth through three routes. (a) pH-conditional lethality. (b) Respiratory failure via vacuolar cysteine storage and iron limitation (Hughes 2020, verified full text). (c) Fet3 copper loading, which needs an assembled V-ATPase, so high-affinity iron uptake fails without it (Davis-Kaplan 2004, verified abstract).
- Route (c) is the only one this model can express without inventing a new pool or a magnitude. The model already has a single, essential-in-vivo high-affinity iron-uptake reaction with a mandatory biomass sink (inferred from the verified facts above).

- They cite Hughes 2020 as supporting 'high-affinity iron uptake fails without V-ATPase'. Hughes explicitly rules out impaired iron uptake: total intracellular iron did not decline and was elevated (ICP-MS). The iron limitation is about bioavailability, not uptake.
- O2a cites Milgrom 2007 and Diab & Kane 2013 for 'iron-dependent respiratory failure'. Neither abstract shows respiratory failure. Milgrom excludes respiration as the main ROS source. Diab & Kane report vma2Δ is iron-replete.

D09277g/D09308g are labelled 'FET3/FTR1'. The locus-map annotation of D09277g is FET5-like (YFL041W), and S. cerevisiae Fet5/Fth1 is a vacuolar-membrane complex (Urbanowski & Piper 1999, abstract verified). Its role as plasma-membrane high-affinity uptake is unverified.
Patterson 2018: the findings say grepping for 'vacuol' returned no hits. The extracted text has 1 hit, about the PRB1 vacuolar protease and not the V-ATPase. The conclusion is unaffected.

Davis-Kaplan 2004: the abstract does not say cwh36 is 'a V0 subunit'. It says 'weak homology to a component of the vacuolar H+-ATPase'. The V0/e identity is recalled. Sambade 2005 (verified) only says it disrupts 'a previously uncharacterized V-ATPase subunit'.

Poltermann 2005: the vma4, vma10 and tfp1 null statements (PMIDs 31542189, 25220074) were not checked this run. Only the vma7 abstract was verified. 'Avirulent in mouse models' is verified for vma7 only.
Raines 2013: 'stv1 null has no phenotype' overstates the abstract, which says only the tested V-ATPase, vacuolar and in vitro virulence-related phenotypes were unaffected.
Inferred claim 'obligate aerobe, so V-ATPase loss is lethal': the M. oryzae Movma11 null (an obligate aerobe) is viable (Chen 2013, verified), so this inference is not general across fungi.

The literature mechanism list omits two verified-abstract alternatives. Sambade 2005 proposes constitutive calcineurin activation as 'the predominant physiological basis of the Vma- growth phenotype'. Ohya 1991 reports that Pet- cls (vma) mutants 'showed no detectable mitochondrial defects'. Both weaken a single iron/respiration explanation.
missing: No source shows that V-ATPase knockout is lethal (as opposed to strongly depleted) in Y. lipolytica. The evidence is pooled 4-day log2 depletion only, and the mapping from FS to KO/WT < 15% is not established.

CCC2-like YALI1D35635g (Golgi Cu-ATPase for Fet3 copper loading) is consensus-essential (verified). It is the one Y. lipolytica datum consistent with a secretory-pathway copper-loading requirement, and the findings did not use it.

The Y. lipolytica genome annotates alternative iron-entry homologs that are absent from m059: SMF1-like C05880g, SMF3-like D35356g, FTR1-like A05031g, five ARN1-like siderophore transporters, and A21283g, weakly similar to FET3. Any V-ATPase AND on R2193 ignores them. All are non-essential in the screens (verified for C05880g, D35356g, A05031g and A21283g).
Which a-isoform (STV1-like E12482g or VPH1-like F38820g) serves Fet3/Fet5 maturation is unknown. O2a's 11-of-11 variant depends on it.

SD-Leu iron and copper content and the culture pH were not opened from any source. YNB's FeCl3 content is recalled only. Whether the screen medium is iron-limiting, which is the condition under which Davis-Kaplan's defect appears, is unverified.
Full texts of Davis-Kaplan 2004, Milgrom 2007, Diab & Kane 2013, Kane 2006 (HTTP 403) and Patterson Table S3 were not read. Only the abstracts were read (Patterson main text was read).
